transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I guess I’m here because I can’t seem to stop starting things. Like at work I’ll come up with these big plans—new workflows, certification tracks, system upgrades—and then at home it’s the same thing, like redoing the whole network or reaching out to people I haven’t talked to in years.

It sounds productive, and sometimes it is, but it gets… too much. I keep pushing past normal stopping points. My wife will be like, “You need to stop,” or my director has to step in and tell me I’m overloading everyone. And I know that’s probably why I’m here, even though part of me still feels like I’m just trying to get things moving.
When this gets going, do you find that you need much less sleep than usual?

Yeah… when it gets going, I don’t seem to need much. Like there’ve been stretches where I’ll sleep maybe three hours, and then I’m awake at 3 or 4 in the morning, just… sharp. Not groggy.

And it’s weird because normally if someone wakes me up that early I’m useless, but then it feels like I got handed extra hours in the day. Like bonus time. I’ll start thinking, “Okay, I can knock out those emails, organize that folder structure,” or whatever, and then suddenly it’s morning.
When you’re in these high-energy periods, have you ever heard or seen things that other people didn’t, or become convinced of something that others said wasn’t true?

Yeah… I mean, not like seeing a person standing there or anything, but during the really driven stretches—when I’m barely sleeping and I’ve got all these big plans going—I start noticing things that feel… pointed.

Like the server room noise, the fans and drives, I’d swear I could hear comments in it. Not full conversations exactly, more like little remarks, like it was reacting to what I was doing. And then at work, messages from people—normal emails or chat updates—I’d read them and feel like there were hidden threats in there, like they were warning me or trying to corner me.

It’s hard to explain because part of me knows it sounds strange, but at the time it feels connected. Like when you’re troubleshooting a network issue and suddenly every log line seems important, except it’s people’s messages and background noise, and I can’t always tell what’s signal and what’s just… noise.
Do those experiences with the server-room noises or hidden messages happen only when you're in one of those high-energy, low-sleep stretches?

No… not only then. That’s the part that makes it harder to explain, I guess.

There have been calmer stretches too, like a few weeks where I wasn’t especially wired or down, just kind of flat, going to work, doing the normal routine. And I’d still catch myself thinking Teams statuses meant something coded, like a warning or a signal. Like someone putting “busy” or “available” at a certain time wasn’t just normal office stuff.

And the sounds… yeah, sometimes I’d still hear these brief comments when nobody was there. Not a whole conversation, just quick little remarks. I know the server room is noisy anyway—honestly those fans can make all kinds of patterns if you listen too long—but it wasn’t only during the low-sleep times.
Have there been at least two weeks when you were not unusually energized or depressed, but still heard those brief comments or believed messages had hidden meanings?

Yeah… yes. I mean, that’s happened. There have been a few stretches like that, a few weeks at a time, where I wasn’t really up, not running on no sleep or feeling amazing, and I wasn’t especially depressed either. More just flat, doing the normal work routine.

But even then I’d still get stuck on things like Teams statuses, like “busy” or “available” showing up at a certain time, and I’d feel like it was some kind of coded warning. Which sounds ridiculous when I say it out loud, because I manage systems and I know statuses are just statuses most of the time… but it would still feel aimed at me.

And the brief comments too, yeah. Like hearing a quick remark when nobody was there. Not constant, not like a big scene, but enough that I’d stop and look around. So… yes, at least two weeks, definitely.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Yeah… yes, I think so. There are stretches where I wake up and it’s like I’m already behind before anything has even happened. Just this heavy, flat feeling, like I’m some failed version of myself.

And it’s most of the day, not just a bad morning. Even my wife asking normal things—like what I want for dinner or whether I paid something—feels like too much to answer. Which sounds stupid, because it’s just a question, but in those periods it feels like I don’t have the energy to be a normal person in my own house.

Sorry, I’m kind of circling it. But yes, at least two weeks, where it’s there nearly every day.
Have you ever been hospitalized because of one of these high-energy periods?

I’m not sure how to answer that cleanly. I don’t think I have a clear “yes, that was for a high-energy stretch” kind of thing to point to.

There have been times people around me were really worried, and it felt like everything was moving too fast, but hospitalization specifically… I don’t know, I don’t want to say yes if that’s not right. Hospitals make me think of my dad’s surgery years ago, and how the lighting was awful and nobody could ever explain the parking garage validation thing—sorry, that’s not what you asked.

I guess the honest answer is: I’m not sure, or I don’t have a clear hospitalization because of that to tell you about.
Have you ever had a manic period without hearing those comments or thinking messages had hidden meanings?

I don’t think so… or at least, not the really driven ones.

When I’m in those stretches where I’m barely sleeping and I’m pushing these huge plans, like reorganizing everything or thinking I’ve got some breakthrough at work, that’s usually also when I start hearing little comments in the server noise. Like the hum or clicks feel like they’re saying something. And work messages start feeling… not just like messages, but like there are hidden threats in them.

Sorry, I’m thinking of this one time with a ticket queue and the wording was probably totally normal, but I kept rereading it like it was aimed at me. So, no, I can’t really separate them. The big high-energy periods usually had that stuff mixed in.
At any time, have you had at least two weeks of hearing those brief comments or thinking messages had hidden meanings while your mood felt normal—not unusually high and not depressed?

Yeah… yes, I think that’s happened.

It’s not always tied to me being revved up or really low. There have been stretches where I’d describe my mood as kind of normal, or maybe just flat, but not depressed exactly and not high. Like I was going to work, doing the basic stuff, not sleeping weirdly or taking on some huge project.

But I’d still see Teams statuses and feel like they weren’t just normal away/busy things, like they were coded warnings or meant for me somehow. Which sounds ridiculous when I say it out loud, because it’s just a little colored dot and a status message, and I manage systems for a living, so I know how those things work. But at the time it felt like there was a pattern.

And I’d still hear brief comments sometimes when nobody was there. Not long conversations, just quick little remarks. That has gone on for a few weeks at a time, even when my mood wasn’t especially up or down.
